# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Melillo_2023_gadoxetate_rat_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Melillo_2023_gadoxetate_rat_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics15030896> (open access, PMC10057977)
* Gadoxetate PBPK backbone: Scotcher et al. 2021,
  <https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.1c00206>

Gadoxetate is a hepatobiliary MRI contrast agent taken up into hepatocytes by
OATP (rat Oatp1b2) and excreted into bile by MRP2 (rat Mrp2). Melillo et al.
used it as an imaging biomarker to probe hepatic transporter drug--drug
interactions in rats: for six perpetrator drugs they predicted, *prospectively*,
the change in gadoxetate exposure in plasma and liver from in vitro inhibition
data, and compared the predictions with the observed dynamic contrast-enhanced
MRI (DCE-MRI) data.

The packaged model couples the reduced gadoxetate PBPK model of Scotcher 2021
(seven compartments, permeability-limited liver) with empirical compartmental PK
models of five of the perpetrators (rifampicin, asunaprevir, ciclosporin,
pioglitazone, bosentan), each fitted to digitised literature rat PK data
(Supplementary Section S1). Each perpetrator's unbound plasma concentration
inhibits gadoxetate active hepatic uptake and biliary excretion through Equation
2 of the paper,

$$\mathrm{CL_{transporter,inh}} = \frac{\mathrm{CL_{transporter}}}{1 + c_{u,p}(t)/\mathrm{IC_{50}}},$$

with the in vitro IC50 values of Tables 2 and 3. Ketoconazole has no fitted PK
model (its rat PK was read directly from the literature) and so is not
represented. This is a *prediction* model, not a fit to the imaging data; its
single answer key is the paper's own predicted AUC-ratio column of Table 4.

# Population

Male Wistar rats (approximately 250 g) were imaged at four sites and two field
strengths (4.7 T and 7 T). On the first occasion each rat received 25 umol/kg
gadoxetate intravenously after vehicle (control phase); 48 h later the procedure
was repeated 30 or 60 min after a single intravenous perpetrator dose
(inhibitory phase; Table 1). The PBPK model describes the average 250 g rat of
Scotcher 2021 and carries no between-animal variability. The perpetrator PK
models were fitted to published rat PK data (Table S1), not to the imaging
animals.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Melillo_2023_gadoxetate_rat_pbpk")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Quantity | `ini()` name(s) | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gadoxetate CLuptake, CLbiliary, PS | `lps_act_inf`, `lcl_bile`, `lps_remainder` | Tables S10/S11 (Scotcher 2021 Table 3 control fit) |
| Gadoxetate CLpassive, fu,hep, CLr | `lps_dif`, `fu_liver_cell`, `lcl_renal` | Scotcher 2021 Table 3 |
| Rat physiology (volumes, flows, Hct, QCO) | constants in `model()` | Scotcher 2021 Table S2 and Section 5 |
| Relaxivities (blood 6.4/6.2, hepatocytes 7.6/6 per s per mM at 4.7/7 T) | constants in `model()` | Scotcher 2021 Table 1 |
| Rifampicin 1-cmt PK (k10, V1) | `lkel_rif`, `lvc_rif` | Table S2 |
| Asunaprevir 2-cmt PK | `lkel_asv`, `lk12_asv`, `lk21_asv`, `lvc_asv` | Table S3 |
| Ciclosporin 3-cmt PK + RBC binding | `lkel_ciclosporin` ... `lvc_ciclosporin`, `kd_ciclosporin`, `lbmax_ciclosporin` | Tables S4, Eq S11 |
| Pioglitazone 1-cmt PK + oral depot | `lka_pioglitazone`, `lfdepot_pioglitazone`, `lkel_pioglitazone`, `lvc_pioglitazone` | Table S5 |
| Bosentan 2-cmt PK | `lkel_bosentan`, `lk12_bosentan`, `lk21_bosentan`, `lvc_bosentan` | Table S6 |
| Perpetrator plasma fu | `fu_rif`, `fu_asv`, `fu_ciclosporin`, `fu_pioglitazone`, `fu_bosentan` | Table 3 (fu column) |
| In vitro IC50 (uptake / biliary) | `ki_oatp_*`, `ki_mrp2_*` | Tables 2 and 3 (see Errata) |
| Equation 2 inhibition; Equation 1 liver ODEs | n/a | Equations 1-2; Scotcher 2021 equation system S1 |

# Simulation

The perpetrators are dosed in micromoles, converted from the mg/kg doses of
Table 1 for the 250 g rat with the molar masses below. Gadoxetate is given as a
25 umol/kg (= 6.25 umol) 30-s intravenous infusion into `blood`, staggered after
the perpetrator by the Table 1 interval. Pioglitazone was given intravenously in
the imaging study, so it is dosed straight into `central_pioglitazone` (its oral
depot is left unused).

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Melillo_2023_gadoxetate_rat_pbpk")

bw <- 0.25 # kg, reference rat
gd_umol <- 25 * bw # 25 umol/kg gadoxetate

# Perpetrator molar masses (g/mol) for the mg/kg -> umol conversion.
mw <- c(
  rif = 822.94, asv = 748.3, ciclosporin = 1202.6,
  pioglitazone = 356.44, bosentan = 551.6
)

# Table 1 scenarios: drug suffix, mg/kg dose, staggering interval (min).
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~label, ~mgkg, ~stag_min,
  "rif", "Rifampicin 2 mg/kg", 2, 60,
  "rif", "Rifampicin 10 mg/kg", 10, 60,
  "ciclosporin", "Ciclosporin 5 mg/kg", 5, 60,
  "asv", "Asunaprevir 5 mg/kg", 5, 30,
  "pioglitazone", "Pioglitazone 0.4 mg/kg", 0.4, 30,
  "bosentan", "Bosentan 2 mg/kg", 2, 60,
  "bosentan", "Bosentan 4-6 mg/kg", 5, 60
)

# Events: perpetrator IV bolus at t = 0 (inhibitory arm only), gadoxetate
# 30-s infusion at the staggering time, dense observation grid over the 25-min
# imaging window that starts with the gadoxetate dose.
make_events <- function(drug, mgkg, stag_min, treated) {
  t0 <- stag_min / 60
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = gd_umol, cmt = "blood", time = t0, dur = 30 / 3600)
  if (treated) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(
      ev,
      amt = mgkg * bw / mw[[drug]] * 1000,
      cmt = paste0("central_", drug), time = 0
    )
  }
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, seq(t0, t0 + 25 / 60, by = 1 / 3600))
  as.data.frame(ev)
}

solve_arm <- function(drug, label, mgkg, stag_min, treated) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, make_events(drug, mgkg, stag_min, treated),
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  t0 <- stag_min / 60
  s <- s[s$time >= t0 - 1e-9, ]
  s$tmin <- (s$time - t0) * 60 # minutes since gadoxetate dose
  s$label <- label
  s$arm <- ifelse(treated, "treated", "control")
  s
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    solve_arm(scen$drug[i], scen$label[i], scen$mgkg[i], scen$stag_min[i], FALSE),
    solve_arm(scen$drug[i], scen$label[i], scen$mgkg[i], scen$stag_min[i], TRUE)
  )
}))
```

## Gadoxetate Delta R1 profiles (Figures 3, 4, 6)

The imaging signal is Delta R1 (1/s), linear in tissue concentration through the
relaxivities. The liver profile falls, and the plasma (spleen) profile rises, in
the inhibitory arms of the strong OATP inhibitors ciclosporin and rifampicin,
while the other drugs overlie their controls -- the qualitative result of
Figures 3, 4 and 6.

```{r profiles, fig.height = 6}
prof <- sim |>
  dplyr::select(label, arm, tmin, dR1_liver_4p7t, dR1_spleen_4p7t) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(dR1_liver_4p7t, dR1_spleen_4p7t),
    names_to = "tissue", values_to = "dR1"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tissue = ifelse(grepl("liver", tissue), "Liver", "Plasma (spleen)"))

ggplot(prof, aes(tmin, dR1, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(tissue ~ label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time since gadoxetate dose (min)", y = "Delta R1 (1/s) at 4.7 T",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Prospective AUC-ratio prediction (Table 4)

The paper's endpoint is the gadoxetate AUC ratio (AUCR, Equation 3): the ratio of
the treated to control AUC of the Delta R1-time profile, in plasma (from the
spleen compartment) and in liver, integrated over the 25-min imaging window. The
block below reproduces the *predicted* AUCR column of Table 4.

```{r aucr}
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

aucr_tab <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(label, arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    plasma = trap(time, dR1_spleen_4p7t),
    liver = trap(time, dR1_liver_4p7t),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(plasma, liver)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    label,
    `Plasma AUCR (model)` = round(plasma_treated / plasma_control, 2),
    `Liver AUCR (model)` = round(liver_treated / liver_control, 2)
  )

# Predicted AUCR reported by Melillo 2023 Table 4 (plasma; liver).
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label, ~`Plasma AUCR (Table 4)`, ~`Liver AUCR (Table 4)`,
  "Rifampicin 2 mg/kg", 1.15, 0.98,
  "Rifampicin 10 mg/kg", 1.62, 0.90,
  "Ciclosporin 5 mg/kg", 3.39, 0.38,
  "Asunaprevir 5 mg/kg", 1.01, 1.00,
  "Pioglitazone 0.4 mg/kg", 1.00, 1.00,
  "Bosentan 2 mg/kg", 1.00, 1.00,
  "Bosentan 4-6 mg/kg", 1.00, 1.00
)

cmp <- dplyr::left_join(aucr_tab, published, by = "label")
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Predicted gadoxetate AUCR: model vs Melillo 2023 Table 4.")
```

```{r aucr-check}
# The model is deterministic; its only approximation versus the paper is the
# digitised staggering/injection timing, so a 15% band around each published
# predicted AUCR is a strict structural check (a transcription error in any
# perpetrator PK parameter, fu, IC50, dose or the inhibition equation moves a
# ratio far outside it).
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cmp$`Plasma AUCR (model)` - cmp$`Plasma AUCR (Table 4)`) /
    cmp$`Plasma AUCR (Table 4)` < 0.15),
  all(abs(cmp$`Liver AUCR (model)` - cmp$`Liver AUCR (Table 4)`) /
    cmp$`Liver AUCR (Table 4)` < 0.15)
)

# Ciclosporin: the paper reports 97-98% inhibition of active uptake during the
# imaging window (Discussion). Confirm the minimum fraction of uptake activity
# remaining in the ciclosporin arm is 2-3%.
csa_uptake_remaining <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(label == "Ciclosporin 5 mg/kg", arm == "treated") |>
  dplyr::pull(f_uptake_remaining) |>
  min()
stopifnot(csa_uptake_remaining > 0.01, csa_uptake_remaining < 0.04)
```

Every predicted AUCR reproduces to within 15% of Table 4, and the four negative
controls (asunaprevir, pioglitazone, both bosentan doses) predict essentially no
interaction, exactly as the paper reports.

# PKNCA cross-check of gadoxetate systemic exposure

As an independent handle on the systemic gadoxetate kinetics, the block below
runs PKNCA on the control-arm blood concentration `Cc` and confirms the plasma
AUCR for the strongest inhibitor (ciclosporin) matches the trapezoidal value
above. PKNCA here operates on the gadoxetate blood concentration, not the Delta
R1 signal.

```{r pknca}
nca_src <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(label == "Ciclosporin 5 mg/kg") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = ifelse(arm == "control", 1L, 2L),
    arm, time = tmin / 60, Cc
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_src, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = c(1L, 2L), arm = c("control", "treated"), time = 0, amt = gd_umol)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, route = "intravascular")

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 25 / 60, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca <- as.data.frame(res$result)

nca_tab <- nca |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = arm, names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename("Cmax (umol/L)" = cmax, "AUClast (umol*h/L)" = auclast)
knitr::kable(nca_tab, caption = "PKNCA of gadoxetate blood Cc, ciclosporin scenario.")

plasma_aucr_nca <- nca$PPORRES[nca$PPTESTCD == "auclast" & nca$arm == "treated"] /
  nca$PPORRES[nca$PPTESTCD == "auclast" & nca$arm == "control"]
# The blood-concentration AUCR and the Delta R1 plasma AUCR of Table 4 both
# measure the rise in systemic gadoxetate from blocked hepatic uptake; they
# agree closely because blood Delta R1 is linear in blood Cc.
stopifnot(abs(plasma_aucr_nca - 3.39) / 3.39 < 0.2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations / Errata

* **Gadoxetate transporter parameters.** The model uses the control-phase
  top-down fit of Scotcher 2021 (Table 3: CLuptake 2.17, CLbiliary 0.07 L/h),
  the values Melillo 2023 Table S11 cites as its gadoxetate baseline. The
  companion `Scotcher_2021_gadoxetate_rat_pbpk` model carries the same structure
  and its other parameter sets.
* **IC50 selection (ciclosporin).** Reproducing Table 4 requires the ciclosporin
  active-uptake inhibition constant to be the human OATP1B1 Ki of 0.014 uM (the
  lowest reported value, Table 3), **not** the rat rOatp1b2 IC50 of 1.2 uM. The
  rat value gives only about 35% uptake inhibition, whereas the paper reports
  97-98% inhibition of CLactive (Discussion) and a liver AUCR of 0.38 (Table 4),
  both of which the human Ki reproduces. Supplementary Section S1.3 motivates the
  low value by ciclosporin's strong OATP1B pre-incubation effect. The biliary
  constant is the median human MRP2 IC50 of 2.7 uM (Figure S11: "<25% inhibition
  of CLbiliary"). Rifampicin, by contrast, reproduces Table 4 with its rat
  rOatp1b2 IC50 of 0.79 uM and rat rMrp2 IC50 of 20 uM, so the choice of rat vs
  human surrogate is drug-specific; the maintainers fixed each perpetrator's
  values to the set that reproduces the paper's own predictions.
* **Perpetrator unbound fractions.** `fu` values are the Table 3 column;
  pioglitazone (`<0.01`) and bosentan (`<0.02`) are reported only as upper
  bounds, taken here at the bound. Because both drugs are predicted (and
  observed) to cause no interaction, the AUCR is insensitive to the exact value.
* **Ciclosporin molar mass.** The red-cell binding equation (Eq S11) is written
  in ug/mL; converting the model's umol/L concentrations needs ciclosporin's
  molar mass (1202.6 g/mol, PubChem CID 5284373), which the paper does not print.
* **Ketoconazole** is omitted: the paper fitted no compartmental PK model for it
  (Supplementary Section S1.4 reads its rat PK from the literature), and its
  predicted AUCR is 1.00.
* **Perpetrator PK equations.** Two supplementary equations are transcribed as
  the structurally correct form rather than as printed: Eq S1's central-input
  term is `ka * AG` (the depot), as in Eq S3, not `ka * A1`; Eq S8's inflow is
  `k13 * A1`, not `k13 * A3`.
* **Determinism.** No between-animal variability or residual error was estimated
  (a prospective prediction), so the model has no `eta`/`sigma` terms.
